celaleyn:1-1.t: ﴿ص﴾ Allah knows best what He means by it. ﴿وَالْقُرْآنِ ذِي الذِّكْرِ﴾ i.e. of clarity, or of honour. The jawāb (answer) of this oath is omitted, i.e. the matter is not as the disbelievers of Mecca said regarding the multiplicity of gods.

celaleyn:2-2.t: ﴿بَلِ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ of the people of Mecca ﴿فِي عِزَّةٍ﴾ zealous pride and arrogance against faith ﴿وَشِقَاقٍ﴾ opposition and enmity towards the Prophet ﷺ.

celaleyn:3-3.t: ﴿كَمْ﴾ i.e. many ﴿أَهْلَكْنَا مِنْ قَبْلِهِمْ مِنْ قَرْنٍ﴾ i.e. a nation among the past nations ﴿فَنَادَوْا﴾ when the punishment descended upon them ﴿وَلَاتَ حِينَ مَنَاصٍ﴾ i.e. the time is not a time of escape. The tāʾ is redundant (zāʾida), and the clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of the fāʿil (agent) of "نَادَوْا", i.e. they cried for help while there was no refuge and no deliverance. And the disbelievers of Mecca did not take a lesson from them. [Translator's note: the printed text reads «اغْتَبَرَ»; the sense requires «اعْتَبَرَ» ("take a lesson"), which is how it is translated here.]

celaleyn:4-4.t: ﴿وَعَجِبُوا أَنْ جَاءَهُمْ مُنْذِرٌ مِنْهُمْ﴾ a messenger from among themselves who warns them and makes them fear the Fire after the resurrection, and he is the Prophet ﷺ. ﴿وَقَالَ الْكَافِرُونَ﴾ In it there is the placing of the overt noun in the position of the pronoun. ﴿هَذَا سَاحِرٌ كَذَّابٌ﴾

celaleyn:5-5.t: ﴿أَجَعَلَ الْآلِهَةَ إِلَهًا وَاحِدًا﴾ when he said to them, "Say: there is no god but Allah", i.e. how can a single god suffice for all creation? ﴿إِنَّ هَذَا لَشَيْءٌ عُجَابٌ﴾ i.e. astonishing.

celaleyn:6-6.t: ﴿وَانْطَلَقَ الْمَلَأُ مِنْهُمْ﴾ from the place of their gathering at Abū Ṭālib's and their hearing there from the Prophet ﷺ, "Say: there is no god but Allah" ﴿أَنِ امْشُوا﴾ i.e. some of them saying to others, "Go on" ﴿وَاصْبِرُوا عَلَى آلِهَتِكُمْ﴾ remain firm in their worship ﴿إِنَّ هَذَا﴾ the affirmation of oneness (tawḥīd) just mentioned ﴿لَشَيْءٌ يُرَادُ﴾ of us.

celaleyn:7-7.t: ﴿مَا سَمِعْنَا بِهَذَا فِي الْمِلَّةِ الْآخِرَةِ﴾ i.e. the religion of ʿĪsā ﴿إِنْ﴾ not ﴿هَذَا إِلَّا اخْتِلَاقٌ﴾ a lie.

celaleyn:8-8.t: ﴿أَأُنْزِلَ﴾ with full pronunciation (taḥqīq) of both hamzas, and with easing (tashīl) of the second, and with the insertion of an alif between them in both ways, and without it ﴿عَلَيْهِ﴾ upon Muḥammad ﴿الذِّكْرُ﴾ the Quran ﴿مِنْ بَيْنِنَا﴾ while he is not the greatest or the noblest of us? i.e. it has not been sent down upon him. The Exalted said: ﴿بَلْ هُمْ فِي شَكٍّ مِنْ ذِكْرِي﴾ My revelation, i.e. the Quran, since they called the one who brought it a liar ﴿بَلْ لَمَّا﴾ not [yet] ﴿يَذُوقُوا عَذَابِ﴾ and if they had tasted it they would have believed the Prophet ﷺ in what he brought; but believing will not benefit them then.

celaleyn:9-9.t: ﴿أَمْ عِنْدَهُمْ خَزَائِنُ رَحْمَةِ رَبِّكَ الْعَزِيزِ﴾ the Dominant ﴿الْوَهَّابِ﴾ of prophethood and other things, so that they give it to whomever they wish?

celaleyn:10-10.t: ﴿أَمْ لَهُمْ مُلْكُ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا﴾ If they claim that, ﴿فَلْيَرْتَقُوا فِي الْأَسْبَابِ﴾ that lead to heaven, and bring the revelation, and assign it to whomever they wish. "أَمْ" in both places has the meaning of the hamza of denial (inkār).

celaleyn:11-11.t: ﴿جُنْدٌ مَا﴾ i.e. a contemptible host ﴿هُنَالِكَ﴾ in their calling you a liar ﴿مَهْزُومٌ﴾ a ṣifa (adjective) of "جُنْدٌ" ﴿مِنَ الْأَحْزَابِ﴾ also a ṣifa of "جُنْدٌ", i.e. like the hosts of the same kind as the factions who banded together against the prophets before you; and those were subdued and destroyed, so likewise We will destroy these.

celaleyn:12-12.t: ﴿كَذَّبَتْ قَبْلَهُمْ قَوْمُ نُوحٍ﴾ the feminine [of the verb] with "قَوْم" is by consideration of the meaning ﴿وَعَادٌ وَفِرْعَوْنُ ذُو الْأَوْتَادِ﴾ for everyone he was angry with, he used to drive in four stakes, to which he tied his hands and feet, and he would torture him.

celaleyn:13-13.t: ﴿وَثَمُودُ وَقَوْمُ لُوطٍ وَأَصْحَابُ الْأَيْكَةِ﴾ the thicket; they are the people of Shuʿayb, peace be upon him ﴿أُولَئِكَ الْأَحْزَابُ﴾

celaleyn:14-14.t: ﴿إِنْ﴾ not ﴿كُلٌّ﴾ of the factions ﴿إِلَّا كَذَّبَ الرُّسُلَ﴾ because when they called one of them a liar, they called all of them liars, since their call is one, namely the call to the oneness of Allah (tawḥīd) ﴿فَحَقَّ﴾ became due ﴿عِقَابِ﴾

celaleyn:15-15.t: ﴿وَمَا يَنْظُرُ﴾ await ﴿هَؤُلَاءِ﴾ the disbelievers of Mecca ﴿إِلَّا صَيْحَةً وَاحِدَةً﴾ it is the blast of the Resurrection, with which the punishment befalls them ﴿مَا لَهَا مِنْ فَوَاقٍ﴾ with fatḥa and ḍamma on the fāʾ: any return.

celaleyn:16-16.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا﴾ when {فَأَمَّا مَنْ أُوتِيَ كِتَابَهُ بِيَمِينِهِ} etc. was revealed: ﴿رَبَّنَا عَجِّلْ لَنَا قِطَّنَا﴾ the record of our deeds ﴿قَبْلَ يَوْمِ الْحِسَابِ﴾ They said that mockingly.

celaleyn:17-17.t: The Exalted said: ﴿اصْبِرْ عَلَى مَا يَقُولُونَ وَاذْكُرْ عَبْدَنَا دَاوُدَ ذَا الْأَيْدِ﴾ i.e. strength in worship. He used to fast one day and break his fast one day, and stand [in prayer] for half the night, sleep a third of it, and stand for a sixth of it. ﴿إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ﴾ one who constantly returns to what pleases Allah.

celaleyn:18-18.t: ﴿إِنَّا سَخَّرْنَا الْجِبَالَ مَعَهُ يُسَبِّحْنَ﴾ with his glorification ﴿بِالْعَشِيِّ﴾ at the time of the ʿishāʾ prayer ﴿وَالْإِشْرَاقِ﴾ at the time of ḍuḥā (forenoon), which is when the sun has risen and its light has reached its full extent.

celaleyn:19-19.t: ﴿وَ﴾ We subjected ﴿الطَّيْرَ مَحْشُورَةً﴾ gathered to him, glorifying with him ﴿كُلٌّ﴾ of the mountains and the birds ﴿لَهُ أَوَّابٌ﴾ constantly returning to obedience to him through glorification.

celaleyn:20-20.t: ﴿وَشَدَدْنَا مُلْكَهُ﴾ We strengthened it with guards and soldiers; thirty thousand men used to guard his miḥrāb every night ﴿وَآتَيْنَاهُ الْحِكْمَةَ﴾ prophethood and soundness of judgement in affairs ﴿وَفَصْلَ الْخِطَابِ﴾ clear and satisfying speech in every purpose.

celaleyn:21-21.t: ﴿وَهَلْ﴾ the meaning of the interrogative here is wonder and the arousing of eagerness to hear what follows ﴿أَتَاكَ﴾ O Muḥammad ﴿نَبَأُ الْخَصْمِ إِذْ تَسَوَّرُوا الْمِحْرَابَ﴾ the miḥrāb of Dāwūd, i.e. his place of worship, since they were prevented from entering upon him through the door because of his being occupied with worship; i.e. [has there come to you] their news and their story?

celaleyn:22-22.t: ﴿إِذْ دَخَلُوا عَلَى دَاوُدَ فَفَزِعَ مِنْهُمْ قَالُوا لَا تَخَفْ﴾ we are ﴿خَصْمَانِ﴾ it is said: two parties, so as to agree with the plural pronoun before it; and it is said: two [persons], with the pronoun according to its meaning, since "خَصْم" is applied to one and to more. They were two angels who came in the form of two litigants, to whom what is mentioned happened by way of a hypothetical case, in order to make Dāwūd, peace be upon him, aware of what had come from him. He had ninety-nine wives, and he asked for the wife of a man who had no one but her, married her and consummated the marriage with her. ﴿بَغَى بَعْضُنَا عَلَى بَعْضٍ فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَنَا بِالْحَقِّ وَلَا تُشْطِطْ﴾ be unjust ﴿وَاهْدِنَا﴾ guide us ﴿إِلَى سَوَاءِ الصِّرَاطِ﴾ the middle of the right path.

celaleyn:23-23.t: ﴿إِنَّ هَذَا أَخِي﴾ i.e. in my religion ﴿لَهُ تِسْعٌ وَتِسْعُونَ نَعْجَةً﴾ by which a woman is expressed ﴿وَلِيَ نَعْجَةٌ وَاحِدَةٌ فَقَالَ أَكْفِلْنِيهَا﴾ make me her guardian ﴿وَعَزَّنِي﴾ he overcame me ﴿فِي الْخِطَابِ﴾ i.e. in argument; and the other acknowledged that.

celaleyn:24-24.t: ﴿قَالَ لَقَدْ ظَلَمَكَ بِسُؤَالِ نَعْجَتِكَ﴾ in order to add her ﴿إِلَى نِعَاجِهِ وَإِنَّ كَثِيرًا مِنَ الْخُلَطَاءِ﴾ partners ﴿لَيَبْغِي بَعْضُهُمْ عَلَى بَعْضٍ إِلَّا الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ وَقَلِيلٌ مَا هُمْ﴾ the "مَا" is to emphasise the fewness. Then the two angels said, as they ascended to heaven in their [own] forms: "The man has passed judgement against himself." So Dāwūd took notice. The Exalted said: ﴿وَظَنَّ﴾ became certain ﴿دَاوُدُ أَنَّمَا فَتَنَّاهُ﴾ We put him to a trial (fitna), i.e. an affliction, through his love for that woman ﴿فَاسْتَغْفَرَ رَبَّهُ وَخَرَّ رَاكِعًا﴾ i.e. prostrating ﴿وَأَنَابَ﴾

celaleyn:25-25.t: ﴿فَغَفَرْنَا لَهُ ذَلِكَ وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَنَا لَزُلْفَى﴾ i.e. an increase of good in this world ﴿وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ﴾ a [good] place of return in the Hereafter.

celaleyn:26-26.t: ﴿يَا دَاوُدُ إِنَّا جَعَلْنَاكَ خَلِيفَةً فِي الْأَرْضِ﴾ managing the affairs of the people ﴿فَاحْكُمْ بَيْنَ النَّاسِ بِالْحَقِّ وَلَا تَتَّبِعِ الْهَوَى﴾ i.e. the desire of the soul ﴿فَيُضِلَّكَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. from the proofs that point to His oneness ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ يَضِلُّونَ عَنْ سَبِيلِ اللَّهِ﴾ i.e. from faith in Allah ﴿لَهُمْ عَذَابٌ شَدِيدٌ بِمَا نَسُوا﴾ for their forgetting ﴿يَوْمَ الْحِسَابِ﴾ on which their abandoning faith was consequent; had they been certain of the Day of Reckoning, they would have believed in this world.

celaleyn:27-27.t: ﴿وَمَا خَلَقْنَا السَّمَاءَ وَالْأَرْضَ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا بَاطِلًا﴾ i.e. in vain ﴿ذَلِكَ﴾ i.e. the creation of what has been mentioned for no purpose ﴿ظَنُّ الَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا﴾ of the people of Mecca ﴿فَوَيْلٌ﴾ a valley ﴿لِلَّذِينَ كَفَرُوا مِنَ النَّارِ﴾

celaleyn:28-28.t: ﴿أَمْ نَجْعَلُ الَّذِينَ آمَنُوا وَعَمِلُوا الصَّالِحَاتِ كَالْمُفْسِدِينَ فِي الْأَرْضِ أَمْ نَجْعَلُ الْمُتَّقِينَ كَالْفُجَّارِ﴾ It was revealed when the disbelievers of Mecca said to the believers, "We will be given in the Hereafter the like of what you are given." "أَمْ" has the meaning of the hamza of denial (inkār).

celaleyn:29-29.t: ﴿كِتَابٌ﴾ the khabar (predicate) of an omitted mubtadaʾ (subject), i.e. "This is" ﴿أَنْزَلْنَاهُ إِلَيْكَ مُبَارَكٌ لِيَدَّبَّرُوا﴾ its original form is "يَتَدَبَّرُوا"; the tāʾ was assimilated into the dāl ﴿آيَاتِهِ﴾ that they consider their meanings and so believe ﴿وَلِيَتَذَكَّرَ﴾ take heed ﴿أُولُو الْأَلْبَابِ﴾ the possessors of intellect.

celaleyn:30-30.t: ﴿وَوَهَبْنَا لِدَاوُدَ سُلَيْمَانَ﴾ his son ﴿نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ﴾ i.e. Sulaymān ﴿إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ﴾ constantly returning in glorification and remembrance at all times.

celaleyn:31-31.t: ﴿إِذْ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ بِالْعَشِيِّ﴾ which is what comes after the sun passes the meridian ﴿الصَّافِنَاتُ﴾ horses, the plural of ṣāfina, which is one standing on three [legs] and setting the other on the edge of the hoof; it is from ṣafana, yaṣfinu, ṣufūnan ﴿الْجِيَادُ﴾ the plural of jawād, which is the one that outruns. The meaning is that when they are made to stand still, they are calm, and when they gallop, they outrun [others]. They were a thousand horses, displayed before him after he had prayed ẓuhr, because he intended to wage jihād on them against an enemy. When nine hundred of them had been displayed, the sun set, and he had not prayed ʿaṣr, so he was grieved.

celaleyn:32-32.t: ﴿فَقَالَ إِنِّي أَحْبَبْتُ﴾ i.e. I wanted ﴿حُبَّ الْخَيْرِ﴾ i.e. the horses ﴿عَنْ ذِكْرِ رَبِّي﴾ the ʿaṣr prayer ﴿حَتَّى تَوَارَتْ﴾ i.e. the sun ﴿بِالْحِجَابِ﴾ i.e. it was hidden by what screens it from sight.

celaleyn:33-33.t: ﴿رُدُّوهَا عَلَيَّ﴾ the horses that had been displayed; so they returned them ﴿فَطَفِقَ مَسْحًا﴾ with the sword ﴿بِالسُّوقِ﴾ the plural of sāq (shank) ﴿وَالْأَعْنَاقِ﴾ i.e. he slaughtered them and cut off their legs as a means of drawing near to Allah the Exalted, since he had been occupied by them from the prayer, and he gave their meat in charity. So Allah compensated him with something better and swifter than them, namely the wind, which ran by his command however he wished.

celaleyn:34-34.t: ﴿وَلَقَدْ فَتَنَّا سُلَيْمَانَ﴾ We tested him with the removal of his kingdom. That was because of his marrying a woman he loved, who used to worship an idol in his house without his knowledge. His kingdom was in his ring; he took it off when he wanted to relieve himself and, as was his habit, left it with his wife, called al-Amīna. A jinnī came to her in the form of Sulaymān and took it from her. ﴿وَأَلْقَيْنَا عَلَى كُرْسِيِّهِ جَسَدًا﴾ it was that jinnī, namely Ṣakhr, or another. He sat on the throne of Sulaymān, and the birds and others gathered around him. Sulaymān came out in other than his usual appearance and saw him on his throne, and said to the people, "I am Sulaymān", but they did not recognise him. ﴿ثُمَّ أَنَابَ﴾ Sulaymān returned to his kingdom after some days, by reaching the ring, putting it on and sitting on his throne.

celaleyn:35-35.t: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ اغْفِرْ لِي وَهَبْ لِي مُلْكًا لَا يَنْبَغِي﴾ shall not be ﴿لِأَحَدٍ مِنْ بَعْدِي﴾ i.e. other than me, like {فَمَنْ يَهْدِيهِ مِنْ بَعْدِ اللَّهِ}, i.e. other than Allah. ﴿إِنَّكَ أَنْتَ الْوَهَّابُ﴾

celaleyn:36-36.t: ﴿فَسَخَّرْنَا لَهُ الرِّيحَ تَجْرِي بِأَمْرِهِ رُخَاءً﴾ gentle ﴿حَيْثُ أَصَابَ﴾ wherever he wished,

celaleyn:37-37.t: ﴿وَالشَّيَاطِينَ كُلَّ بَنَّاءٍ﴾ who builds wondrous buildings ﴿وَغَوَّاصٍ﴾ in the sea, bringing out pearls,

celaleyn:38-38.t: ﴿وَآخَرِينَ﴾ of them ﴿مُقَرَّنِينَ﴾ bound ﴿فِي الْأَصْفَادِ﴾ fetters, with their hands joined to their necks. And We said to him:

celaleyn:39-39.t: ﴿هَذَا عَطَاؤُنَا فَامْنُنْ﴾ give from it to whomever you wish ﴿أَوْ أَمْسِكْ﴾ from giving ﴿بِغَيْرِ حِسَابٍ﴾ i.e. there is no reckoning upon you in that.

celaleyn:40-40.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ لَهُ عِنْدَنَا لَزُلْفَى وَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ﴾ Its like has preceded.

celaleyn:41-41.t: ﴿وَاذْكُرْ عَبْدَنَا أَيُّوبَ إِذْ نَادَى رَبَّهُ أَنِّي﴾ i.e. "that I" [بِأَنِّي] ﴿مَسَّنِيَ الشَّيْطَانُ بِنُصْبٍ﴾ with harm ﴿وَعَذَابٍ﴾ pain. He ascribed that to Satan, even though all things are from Allah, out of courtesy towards Him, Exalted is He. And it was said to him:

celaleyn:42-42.t: ﴿ارْكُضْ﴾ strike ﴿بِرِجْلِكَ﴾ the ground. So he struck, and a spring of water gushed forth, and it was said: ﴿هَذَا مُغْتَسَلٌ﴾ water in which you wash ﴿بَارِدٌ وَشَرَابٌ﴾ from which you drink. So he washed and drank, and every illness that was in his inside and outside left him.

celaleyn:43-43.t: ﴿وَوَهَبْنَا لَهُ أَهْلَهُ وَمِثْلَهُمْ مَعَهُمْ﴾ i.e. Allah brought back to life those of his children who had died, and provided him with the like of them ﴿رَحْمَةً﴾ a blessing ﴿مِنَّا وَذِكْرَى﴾ an admonition ﴿لِأُولِي الْأَلْبَابِ﴾ for the possessors of intellect.

celaleyn:44-44.t: ﴿وَخُذْ بِيَدِكَ ضِغْثًا﴾ it is a bundle of grass or of rods ﴿فَاضْرِبْ بِهِ﴾ your wife; he had sworn that he would strike her a hundred blows because she was slow in coming to him one day ﴿وَلَا تَحْنَثْ﴾ by not striking her. So he took a hundred stalks of idhkhir (lemon grass) or something else and struck her with it a single blow. ﴿إِنَّا وَجَدْنَاهُ صَابِرًا نِعْمَ الْعَبْدُ﴾ Ayyūb ﴿إِنَّهُ أَوَّابٌ﴾ constantly returning to Allah the Exalted.

celaleyn:45-45.t: ﴿وَاذْكُرْ عِبَادَنَا إِبْرَاهِيمَ وَإِسْحَاقَ وَيَعْقُوبَ أُولِي الْأَيْدِي﴾ possessors of strength in worship ﴿وَالْأَبْصَارِ﴾ insight in religion. In a reading [it is] [عَبْدَنَا], with "إِبْرَاهِيمُ" as an explication (bayān) of it, and what comes after it conjoined to "عَبْدَنَا".

celaleyn:46-46.t: ﴿إِنَّا أَخْلَصْنَاهُمْ بِخَالِصَةٍ﴾ it is ﴿ذِكْرَى الدَّارِ﴾ the Hereafter, i.e. remembering it and working for it. In a reading it is with iḍāfa (genitive construct), and it is explicative (li-l-bayān).

celaleyn:47-47.t: ﴿وَإِنَّهُمْ عِنْدَنَا لَمِنَ الْمُصْطَفَيْنَ﴾ the chosen ﴿الْأَخْيَارِ﴾ the plural of khayyir, with doubling (tashdīd).

celaleyn:48-48.t: ﴿وَاذْكُرْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ وَالْيَسَعَ﴾ he is a prophet, and the lām is redundant (zāʾida) ﴿وَذَا الْكِفْلِ﴾ there is disagreement about his prophethood; it is said he gave protection (kafala) to a hundred prophets who fled to him from being killed ﴿وَكُلٌّ﴾ i.e. all of them ﴿مِنَ الْأَخْيَارِ﴾ the plural of khayyir, with the heavy [doubled] form.

celaleyn:49-49.t: ﴿هَذَا ذِكْرٌ﴾ for them, with beautiful praise here ﴿وَإِنَّ لِلْمُتَّقِينَ﴾ who include them ﴿لَحُسْنَ مَآبٍ﴾ a [good] place of return in the Hereafter:

celaleyn:50-50.t: ﴿جَنَّاتِ عَدْنٍ﴾ a badal (substitute) or ʿaṭf bayān (explicative apposition) of "حُسْنَ مَآبٍ" ﴿مُفَتَّحَةً لَهُمُ الْأَبْوَابُ﴾ of them,

celaleyn:51-51.t: ﴿مُتَّكِئِينَ فِيهَا﴾ on couches ﴿يَدْعُونَ فِيهَا بِفَاكِهَةٍ كَثِيرَةٍ وَشَرَابٍ﴾

celaleyn:52-52.t: ﴿وَعِنْدَهُمْ قَاصِرَاتُ الطَّرْفِ﴾ restraining their eyes [to look only] at their husbands ﴿أَتْرَابٌ﴾ their ages are one, and they are thirty-three years old; the plural of tirb.

celaleyn:53-53.t: ﴿هَذَا﴾ what has been mentioned ﴿مَا يُوعَدُونَ﴾ in the third person, and in the second person [تُوعَدُونَ] by way of iltifāt (a shift of person) ﴿لِيَوْمِ الْحِسَابِ﴾ i.e. for its sake.

celaleyn:54-54.t: ﴿إِنَّ هَذَا لَرِزْقُنَا مَا لَهُ مِنْ نَفَادٍ﴾ i.e. cessation. The clause is a ḥāl (circumstantial) of "رِزْقُنَا", or a second khabar (predicate) of "إِنَّ", i.e. "continuing" [accusative] or "continuing" [nominative].

celaleyn:55-55.t: ﴿هَذَا﴾ what has been mentioned is for the believers. ﴿وَإِنَّ لِلطَّاغِينَ﴾ resumptive (mustaʾnaf) ﴿لَشَرَّ مَآبٍ﴾

celaleyn:56-56.t: ﴿جَهَنَّمَ يَصْلَوْنَهَا﴾ they enter it ﴿فَبِئْسَ الْمِهَادُ﴾ the bed.

celaleyn:57-57.t: ﴿هَذَا﴾ i.e. the punishment understood from what follows it ﴿فَلْيَذُوقُوهُ حَمِيمٌ﴾ i.e. hot, scalding water ﴿وَغَسَاقٌ﴾ with the light and the doubled form [غَسَّاقٌ]: what flows from the pus of the people of the Fire.

celaleyn:58-58.t: ﴿وَأُخَرُ﴾ with the plural and the singular [آخَرُ] ﴿مِنْ شَكْلِهِ﴾ i.e. like what has been mentioned of the scalding water and the pus ﴿أَزْوَاجٌ﴾ kinds, i.e. their punishment is of various sorts. And it will be said to them, when they enter the Fire with their followers:

celaleyn:59-59.t: ﴿هَذَا فَوْجٌ﴾ a crowd ﴿مُقْتَحِمٌ﴾ entering ﴿مَعَكُمْ﴾ the Fire with violence. Then those who were followed will say: ﴿لَا مَرْحَبًا بِهِمْ﴾ may there be no ease for them ﴿إِنَّهُمْ صَالُو النَّارِ﴾

celaleyn:60-60.t: ﴿قَالُوا﴾ i.e. the followers ﴿بَلْ أَنْتُمْ لَا مَرْحَبًا بِكُمْ أَنْتُمْ قَدَّمْتُمُوهُ﴾ i.e. disbelief ﴿لَنَا فَبِئْسَ الْقَرَارُ﴾ for us and you is the Fire.

celaleyn:61-61.t: ﴿قَالُوا﴾ also ﴿رَبَّنَا مَنْ قَدَّمَ لَنَا هَذَا فَزِدْهُ عَذَابًا ضِعْفًا﴾ i.e. the like of his punishment for his disbelief ﴿فِي النَّارِ﴾

celaleyn:62-62.t: ﴿وَقَالُوا﴾ the disbelievers of Mecca, while they are in the Fire ﴿مَا لَنَا لَا نَرَى رِجَالًا كُنَّا نَعُدُّهُمْ﴾ in the world ﴿مِنَ الْأَشْرَارِ﴾

celaleyn:63-63.t: ﴿أَتَّخَذْنَاهُمْ سُخْرِيًّا﴾ with ḍamma on the sīn and with kasra [سِخْرِيًّا], i.e. we used to mock them in the world; and the yāʾ is for relation (nisba). I.e. are they missing? ﴿أَمْ زَاغَتْ﴾ turned aside ﴿عَنْهُمُ الْأَبْصَارُ﴾ so that we do not see them? They are the poor among the Muslims, such as ʿAmmār, Bilāl, Ṣuhayb and Salmān.

celaleyn:64-64.t: ﴿إِنَّ ذَلِكَ لَحَقٌّ﴾ its occurrence is certain, and it is ﴿تَخَاصُمُ أَهْلِ النَّارِ﴾ as preceded.

celaleyn:65-65.t: ﴿قُلْ﴾ O Muḥammad, to the disbelievers of Mecca: ﴿إِنَّمَا أَنَا مُنْذِرٌ﴾ one who warns of the Fire ﴿وَمَا مِنْ إِلَهٍ إِلَّا اللَّهُ الْوَاحِدُ الْقَهَّارُ﴾ over His creation,

celaleyn:66-66.t: ﴿رَبُّ السَّمَاوَاتِ وَالْأَرْضِ وَمَا بَيْنَهُمَا الْعَزِيزُ﴾ prevailing in His affair ﴿الْغَفَّارُ﴾ to His friends.

celaleyn:68-68.t: ﴿أَنْتُمْ عَنْهُ مُعْرِضُونَ﴾ i.e. the Quran, about which I have informed you, and in which I have brought you what cannot be known except by revelation, namely His saying:

celaleyn:69-69.t: ﴿مَا كَانَ لِيَ مِنْ عِلْمٍ بِالْمَلَإِ الْأَعْلَى﴾ i.e. the angels ﴿إِذْ يَخْتَصِمُونَ﴾ concerning Ādam, when Allah the Exalted said {إِنِّي جَاعِلٌ فِي الْأَرْضِ خَلِيفَةً} etc.

celaleyn:70-70.t: ﴿إِنْ﴾ not ﴿يُوحَى إِلَيَّ إِلَّا أَنَّمَا أَنَا﴾ i.e. that I am ﴿نَذِيرٌ مُبِينٌ﴾ clear in warning. Remember

celaleyn:71-71.t: ﴿إِذْ قَالَ رَبُّكَ لِلْمَلَائِكَةِ إِنِّي خَالِقٌ بَشَرًا مِنْ طِينٍ﴾ he is Ādam.

celaleyn:72-72.t: ﴿فَإِذَا سَوَّيْتُهُ﴾ I have completed him ﴿وَنَفَخْتُ﴾ I have made flow ﴿فِيهِ مِنْ رُوحِي﴾ so that he becomes alive. The attribution of the spirit to Him is an honouring of Ādam; and the spirit is a subtle body by which a human being lives through its permeating him. ﴿فَقَعُوا لَهُ سَاجِدِينَ﴾ a prostration of greeting, by bowing.

celaleyn:73-73.t: ﴿فَسَجَدَ الْمَلَائِكَةُ كُلُّهُمْ أَجْمَعُونَ﴾ In it there are two tawkīds (emphatic words).

celaleyn:74-74.t: ﴿إِلَّا إِبْلِيسَ﴾ he is the father of the jinn, and he was among the angels ﴿اسْتَكْبَرَ وَكَانَ مِنَ الْكَافِرِينَ﴾ in the knowledge of Allah the Exalted.

celaleyn:75-75.t: ﴿قَالَ يَا إِبْلِيسُ مَا مَنَعَكَ أَنْ تَسْجُدَ لِمَا خَلَقْتُ بِيَدَيَّ﴾ i.e. whose creation I undertook [Myself]; and this is an honouring of Ādam, for every created thing is something whose creation Allah undertook. ﴿أَسْتَكْبَرْتَ﴾ now, from prostrating? An interrogative of rebuke. ﴿أَمْ كُنْتَ مِنَ الْعَالِينَ﴾ the arrogant, so that you were too proud to prostrate because you are one of them?

celaleyn:76-76.t: ﴿قَالَ أَنَا خَيْرٌ مِنْهُ خَلَقْتَنِي مِنْ نَارٍ وَخَلَقْتَهُ مِنْ طِينٍ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:77-77.t: ﴿قَالَ فَاخْرُجْ مِنْهَا﴾ i.e. from Paradise, and it is said: from the heavens ﴿فَإِنَّكَ رَجِيمٌ﴾ expelled.

celaleyn:78-78.t: ﴿وَإِنَّ عَلَيْكَ لَعْنَتِي إِلَى يَوْمِ الدِّينِ﴾ the Recompense.

celaleyn:79-79.t: ﴿قَالَ رَبِّ فَأَنْظِرْنِي إِلَى يَوْمِ يُبْعَثُونَ﴾ i.e. the people.

celaleyn:80-80.t: ﴿قَالَ فَإِنَّكَ مِنَ الْمُنْظَرِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:81-81.t: ﴿إِلَى يَوْمِ الْوَقْتِ الْمَعْلُومِ﴾ the time of the first blast.

celaleyn:82-82.t: ﴿قَالَ فَبِعِزَّتِكَ لَأُغْوِيَنَّهُمْ أَجْمَعِينَ﴾ [Translator's note: al-Jalalayn gives no explanation here.]

celaleyn:83-83.t: ﴿إِلَّا عِبَادَكَ مِنْهُمُ الْمُخْلَصِينَ﴾ i.e. the believers.

celaleyn:84-84.t: ﴿قَالَ فَالْحَقَّ وَالْحَقَّ أَقُولُ﴾ with both in the accusative, and with the first in the nominative [فَالْحَقُّ] and the second in the accusative. The accusative of it [the second] is by the verb after it. The accusative of the first is said to be by the mentioned verb; and it is said to be as a maṣdar (verbal noun), i.e. "I establish the truth"; and it is said to be by removal of the particle of the oath. Its nominative is on the basis that it is a mubtadaʾ (subject) whose khabar (predicate) is omitted, i.e. "So the truth is from Me"; and it is said: "So the truth is My oath". And the jawāb (answer) of the oath is:

celaleyn:85-85.t: ﴿لَأَمْلَأَنَّ جَهَنَّمَ مِنْكَ﴾ with your offspring ﴿وَمِمَّنْ تَبِعَكَ مِنْهُمْ﴾ i.e. of the people ﴿أَجْمَعِينَ﴾

celaleyn:86-86.t: ﴿قُلْ مَا أَسْأَلُكُمْ عَلَيْهِ﴾ for conveying the message ﴿مِنْ أَجْرٍ﴾ any fee ﴿وَمَا أَنَا مِنَ الْمُتَكَلِّفِينَ﴾ who fabricate the Quran of their own accord.

celaleyn:87-87.t: ﴿إِنْ هُوَ﴾ i.e. the Quran is not ﴿إِلَّا ذِكْرٌ﴾ an admonition ﴿لِلْعَالَمِينَ﴾ for humans and jinn, those endowed with reason, to the exclusion of the angels.

celaleyn:88-88.t: ﴿وَلَتَعْلَمُنَّ﴾ O disbelievers of Mecca ﴿نَبَأَهُ﴾ the news of its truthfulness ﴿بَعْدَ حِينٍ﴾ i.e. on the Day of Resurrection. "عَلِمَ" has the meaning of "عَرَفَ" ("to know, recognise"), and the lām before it is the lām of an implied oath, i.e. "By Allah".
